source_reasoning: The single threading.Lock is initialized once for the extracted bootstrap emitter. Its critical section encloses the event limit, record limit and cumulative byte limit checks, the complete os.write, and both shared counter updates. A second writer cannot reserve the same last slot while the first writer releases the GIL in os.write.

The thread-local active check precedes lock acquisition. The active flag is set before entering the lock and cleared in finally on success or error. Reentrant emission raises the finite Observer unavailable reason rather than attempting to reacquire a same-thread non-reentrant lock.

Forbidden-sink emission remains before the denial exception; no unrelated guard was removed by the fix. Earlier unchanged input/filter/guard scopes are carried from the original full report, not newly claimed as global review.

The regression saves the original OS write and writes original serialized records to a test-owned pipe. The first writer is held after its check, while retaining the actual lock. The second thread is observed at lock entry in the fixed implementation or at the write seam in a nonserialized mutant; release occurs only after that observation. Finite wait/join/subprocess fuses avoid an unbounded test deadlock. Exact refusal/counter/pipe-byte assertions do not merely inspect a mocked return value.
